To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the top managers of multinationational corporations are the most disciplined and disciplined people, the international artists are the most disciplined but less disciplined people, the global academics are the most undisciplined but disciplined people, and the big investors are the most undiciplined and disciplined people.
the power over rhythm of top and middle managers in global capitalism is based on a combination of two declinations of rhythm power, which are autodirect power and power over others’ time and space.

1) the TCC in the global capitalist economy are characterized by a high degree of autodirect power over their own time and space; 2) they are also characterized by a high power over the time and space of their subordinates and of co-workers; 3) the two forms of power are correlated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
a new form of power, that is power over the time and space of subordinates and co- workers, as a result of the time- space discipline imposed on those at the top of global capitalism.
the time-space discipline and the relative power of the TCC over their time and space, as well as that over the time and space of the people working for them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
top managers, artists, and academics have the power to decide when and how much they move around the world, while their subordinates and colleagues are subject to the norm of international mobility.

top managers, international artists, and global academics are the most privileged social actors in the global economy, and they enjoy the greatest degrees of freedom over their own rhythm, and the greatest power over that of others.

top managers, international artists, and global academics, in the global capitalist system, are all characterized by the power over their own time-space discipline, and by the power over the time-space discipline of their subordinates and/or co-workers, which they exercise through the division of labor and the norm of international mobility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
of the TCC’s power over time-space discipline, which is the power over the rhythm of others and the degree of freedom from the rhythm imposed on oneself.

, in the current stage of global capitalism, the TCC are the main actors of the time-space discipline imposed on the whole of the population, and that they are also, to different degrees, subjected to this discipline themselves, as they are the first to be affected by the new norm of international mobility.

the time and space discipline imposed by the TCC on their subordinates and on the global capitalist division of labor, as a whole, is a form of social power that, in turn, is a key element of the TCC relative geometries of social power in global capitalism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the current phase of global capitalism, the TCC have gained the power over time and that of others, and that this has come at the cost of a growing loss of power over their own time and space.
the power over one’s time and that of others is a key element of power among the upper classes in global capitalism, and it is a key factor in their reproduction as a class.
time-space discipline is not a prerogative of the TCC only, as it is also imposed on those who work for them.
